chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about the hunting of the Magians for the fish when they strike over it with nets, and they name it with Shirk (polytheism). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with their hunting. Indeed, the hunting of fish is catching it.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the enclosure of reeds made in the water for the fish. The fish enter it, so some of them die in it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. Indeed, that enclosure was made to be hunted with it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish caught by Zoroastrians using nets or traps?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of consuming fish caught by Magians, emphasizing that the ritualistic invocation of 'Shirk' does not invalidate the act of hunting since the essence of fish capture is merely physical seizure, distinct from the slaughter of land animals. This ruling extends to passive traps like reed enclosures, clarifying that the method of capture—whether active netting or passive entrapment—does not alter the halal status, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the primary condition for fish is simply being caught in water.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked

about a hunting of the Magians for the fishes when they strike over it with the netting, and they are naming it with the Polytheism (Shirk). So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem with their hunting. But rather, hunting of the fishes is their catching it’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the enclosure of canes made to be in the water for the fishes. The fishes enter into it, so some of them are dying in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. That enclosure, rather it was made to be for hunting with it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked

about the fishing by Zoroastrian by means of fishing nets and with a mention of the pagan consecration expressions. He (the Imam) said, ‘Their fishing is not unlawful; fishing is catching them (alive).’ I then asked about a barricade of reeds with water in it for fish. Fish enters it and certain ones of them die in it. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful; the barricade is set for fishing.’”
